:::{#exm-tte-overview-censoring-bias}
#### Six patients followed for relapse

Suppose a study follows six cancer patients in remission for up to 12 months,
and we want to estimate the 12-month relapse risk,
$1 - \survf{12}$,
where $\surv$ is the [survival function](intro-to-survival-analysis.qmd#def-surv-fn) of time to relapse
(in months).
@tbl-tte-overview-patients shows each patient's observed follow-up time
and event indicator
(1 = relapse observed; 0 = [right-censored](intro-to-survival-analysis.qmd#def-right-censor)).

::: {#tbl-tte-overview-patients}

| Patient | Follow-up time (months) | Event indicator | Relapse status at 12 months |
|:-------:|:-----------------------:|:---------------:|:----------------------------|
| A | 3  | 1 | relapsed |
| B | 5  | 0 | unknown (withdrew) |
| C | 7  | 1 | relapsed |
| D | 9  | 0 | unknown (withdrew) |
| E | 12 | 0 | relapse-free |
| F | 12 | 0 | relapse-free |

Hypothetical follow-up data for six patients

:::

**Naive approach 1: treat censored patients as event-free.**
Counting patients B and D as relapse-free gives
$2/6 \approx 0.333$.
This approach can only *under*estimate the risk,
because any relapses that B or D experienced after withdrawal
are counted as non-relapses.

**Naive approach 2: drop patients with unknown status.**
Discarding patients B and D gives
$2/4 = 0.5$.
This approach throws away the information that B stayed relapse-free for 5 months
and D for 9 months,
so in this example it *over*estimates the risk.

**Using the censored observations.**
The [Kaplan-Meier estimator](intro-to-survival-analysis.qmd#def-KM-estimator)
keeps each censored patient in the [risk set](intro-to-survival-analysis.qmd#def-risk-set)
until their censoring time
[@kleinbaum2012survival, Chapter 2].
Relapses occur at 3 months (6 patients at risk)
and at 7 months (4 patients at risk: C, D, E, F),
so

$$
\ba
\eskmf{12}
&= \paren{1 - \frac{1}{6}} \cdot \paren{1 - \frac{1}{4}}
&& \text{(product over the event times 3 and 7)}
\\
&= \frac{5}{6} \cdot \frac{3}{4}
&& \text{(subtract inside each factor)}
\\
&= \frac{15}{24}
&& \text{(multiply numerators and denominators)}
\\
&= 0.625
&& \text{(divide)}
\ea
$$

and the estimated 12-month risk is
$1 - 0.625 = 0.375$.
That estimate lies between the two naive estimates,
and it is valid under [non-informative censoring](intro-to-survival-analysis.qmd#def-noninformative-censoring)
[@kleinbaum2012survival, Chapter 1].

:::
